text:
The dynamics between Elizabeth Bennet and Mr. Darcy serve as the primary vehicle for exploring the novel's themes of class and social mobility. Their initial mutual disdain stems from their differing social standings and personal flaws—Darcy’s pride and Elizabeth’s prejudice. As they overcome these barriers through self-reflection and a deeper understanding of one another, their evolving relationship demonstrates that genuine connection can transcend rigid societal structures. This transformation underscores the theme that love, when grounded in respect and self-awareness, has the power to challenge and reshape social hierarchies.
